utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I just wish to notify the Trial Chamber that we have submitted a motion to the Appeals Chamber and submitted an appeal regarding the ruling of the Trial Chamber that the examination-in-chief of common witnesses should be carried out by only one Defence counsel, for it is our view that in the case of joint witnesses proposed by all Defence counsel, that each individual Defence counsel is entitled to examine that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. You mean your appeal is about the question of re-examination by the various Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, examination-in-chief, but I think you mainly wish to focus on the question of whether or not various Defence counsel can re-examine one witness because, of course, you have been allowed to cross-examine a witness who has been examined in chief by one Defence counsel. All right. Thank you. Thank you for notifying the Trial Chamber of your appeal. Thank you so much. Before we bring in the next witness, I would like to ask Defence counsel whether they could be so kind as to submit, maybe by next Monday, a consolidated list of witnesses so that we can have a clear picture of how many witnesses are being called for, say, Count 1, and then for each Defence counsel. Count 1 is a count of persecution, of course, involves quite a few Defence counsel and all accused, so we could have just one list for that particular count, and then each Defence counsel could establish his own or her own list, so that we have, as I say, a complete list of witnesses. Good. I think we may now proceed. I wonder whether the next witness could be brought in, Mr. Vlado Alilovic, I think, and there are no protective measures envisaged for this particular witness. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: On reflection, I think it would probably be appropriate, in view of the motion for appeal which has been filed by Counsel Radovic, for the Trial Chamber to issue a written decision on this matter so that the ruling is supported by reasons, and this would probably facilitate the Appeals Chamber in either upholding the appeal or dismissing the appeal. I think it is just for the sake of better proceedings. Yes, Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would agree with you, but we know roughly what your reasoning will be, as you have already explained that to us, so if you will write a written ruling, we have already submitted our appeal, and in any event, this will facilitate the work of the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you so much. Good morning, Mr. Alilovic. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, are you going to examine in chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No. Counsel Susak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Yes, Counsel Susak. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Susak:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Alilovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your first appearance in court?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be asking you some questions today, and I expect you to answer them. So can we begin?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can begin. Let me just have some water, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell us when you were born and where?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in 1948 in Donja Rovna, Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you come to live in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in 1976 and I have been living and working there since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: My occupation is an economist and especially for internal trade, I specialise in internal trade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do before the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in my field, the field I have been trained for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a military man during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not in the military during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you lived in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I lived in Vitez since 1976, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were in Vitez, could you tell us the relationship between the Muslims and Croats there, before the elections and after the elections, so we can make a difference?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The relationships between the Muslims and Croats before the elections were good, relatively good, for at least as far as I know, nothing ever surfaced that could indicate poor relations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I just ask you, Mr. Alilovic, could speak more slowly so that the interpreters can follow? And after the elections ...

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I would say that relations between Muslims and Croats during the elections were also good. One could even say that they may have been better than before the elections for the simple reason that both ethnic groups, aspiring towards democratic changes, used the same methods in the election campaign and very frequently sought jointly to win over as many voters as possible in order to achieve their goal, and that was to get more votes so as to be able to carry out democratic changes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've said what relations were like before and during the elections. Could you tell us now what they were like before the conflict and after the conflict and whether they deteriorated?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Those relations, after the elections, were good for quite some time. In fact, they were good until, after some time, quite opposing views emerged as regards the developments in Yugoslavia or in Bosnia and Herzegovina; that is, until positions were taken regarding the concentration of vast forces of the Yugoslav People's Army, both in manpower and equipment, in Bosnia and Herzegovina and their use for the aggression against Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the relationships between the SDA and the HDZ parties?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I have already said that the relations between the parties during the elections were good and also for a long time after the elections; in fact, all the time I would say that those relations were quite good because party representatives were often in touch with one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we discuss the elections themselves, could you tell us how the population was composed in Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: According to the 1991 census, the population of Vitez was 27.679 inhabitants, out of which 12.679 Croats or 45.7 per cent, Muslims numbered 11.471 or 41.4 per cent, Serbs 1.502 or 5.4 per cent, Yugoslavs 1.362 or 4.9 per cent, others 714 or 2.6 per cent. Among the others, there were some Montenegrins, a few Slovenes, and some Romanies or Gypsies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us now what the election results were.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The elections were held at the end of 1990 and the results were as follows: the Former League of Communists or the SDP won 18.6 per cent of the votes or 2.711 votes; the SDA won 4.470 votes or 30.7 per cent; the HDZ, 5.849 or 40.2 per cent; the SDS, 476 or 3.3 per cent; the Reformist forces, 564 or 3.9 per cent; and the League of Socialist Youth, 306 or 2.1 per cent. There were more than 14.000 voters who participated in the polls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the elections, how were the authorities composed and how did they function and the bodies of government?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but it seems to me that I can't hear the interpreter too well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, increase the volume. You have a button for the volume, plus/minus. Can you hear better now?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how the authorities functioned after the elections?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I know that after the elections, that is the HDZ party won the mandate to form a government, that the government was successfully constituted, and, at the beginning of 1991, it started functioning normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the various government departments formed, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the two most important positions were divided so that Mr. Ivan Santic became president of the municipality, as a representative of the HDZ, and that the president of the executive body was Mr. Fuad Kaknjo, whereas the other positions were shared out to correspond to the results in the elections, and I think that there were no serious problems in that area. On the contrary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of village guards and the Territorial Defence and how it operated at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the village guards began to be formed after the attack on the village of Ravno at the end of 1991 or, rather, at the end of the month of October. In some villages, those guards were at first joint guards because the population in most villages of Vitez municipality was mixed, and those guards, as far as I know, remained operative until the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At first, they were joint?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were jointly composed for some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. So we come to the point when a split occurred. Could you tell us when and how relations between the Muslims and Croats deteriorated and why?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: A deterioration of relations between the Croats and the Muslims occurred, as I have already briefly mentioned in my testimony, when quite opposing views were taken regarding the aggression on Croatia. The Croatian side thought that after the aggression against Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina would become the target of aggression. The official authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or at least the high-level leaders, upheld the view that that was not Bosnia's war and that they were not interested in it but, rather, that this was a war exclusively between Serbs and Croats. When those forces were amassed in large numbers in Bosnia-Herzegovina, both in terms of troops and equipment, the official authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina adopted a decision to remain neutral. As for relationships in Vitez itself, they continued to be maintained at what I would call a satisfactory level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, immediately prior to the outbreak of hostilities, how was arming carried out, or perhaps you could tell us what were the causes that prompted the formation of the Croatian Defence Council, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The causes behind the formation of the Croatian Defence Council were the differences in the approach to defence between the Croats and Muslims and the assessment that, in view of the current military and political situation, something should be done to prepare for defence against the Serbian aggression, and towards the end of 1991 already, people started seriously thinking about preparations for defence, and they acquired the means in various ways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us how they were armed, and let me refresh your memory, could you tell us what you know about Slimena and the Busovaca barracks?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: We were talking about village guards a moment ago, and they were armed with their own personal sidearms, hunting weapons, and some weapons that they managed to get hold of in various ways, most often on the black market. But by the beginning of 1992 already, because of the overall military and political situation, serious thought was given to the need for acquiring larger quantities of weapons, and the only possibility was to regain control of the equipment of the Territorial Defence, which had been placed under the control of the Yugoslav People's Army, and also possibly to capture one of the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army. It was along those lines that activities were undertaken to try and negotiate the surrender of the Busovaca barracks and the capture of the military depot in ^ Slimena that you have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who provided the initiative for taking the weapons in ^ Slimena? I am referring to both Croats and Muslims now.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The initiative came from the Croatian side, that is sure, and that was how preparations were made to capture it. This happened sometime in mid April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this happened, how were those weapons shared out? Were the Muslims given an equal share or not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I know that in that barracks, the entire equipment for the Territorial Defence of Central Bosnia were stored there, which means a very large quantity of weapons. Immediately after the capture of that depot, negotiations started between the Croats and Muslims, and the Muslims insisted on the weapons being shared, and eventually an agreement to that effect was reached. Some of those weapons were certainly destroyed, but the remainder was shared out 50/50. This was done more or less with the weapons that were captured in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was just what I was going to say. Were those weapons shared out 50/50 as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you tell us about the civilian authority? Were there parallel organisations of the Muslims and the Croats, because we already said that after the elections the authorities were formed jointly. Later on a separation occurred, so tell us how that happened. Did this happen by municipalities, did it take place gradually?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: After the depot and the barracks were seized and the weapons captured, the people certainly felt safer should the Serbs decide to commit aggression. Already in April Kupres had been captured and the Yugoslav People's Army forces were already on the slopes of Mount Vlasic. And on the south eastern side and the southwestern, and virtually from all sides, Central Bosnia, in the broadest sense, was closed in, or, in a sense, under blockade, or at least that was the expectation, that it would be blocked. Due to the capture of Kupres and the only road leading out to the world, and the only road that could be used for supply, both supplies of good and other necessities, the Croatian side started thinking how it could address the problem of communication and lift the blockade so as to open the way towards Bosnia and Croatia. The Muslim side, it at the time, adopted a rather passive attitude toward the problem and was inert, and that is why the Croatian people, as a whole, thought about forming the Croatian Defence Council and the highest body for the preparations of the defence and as the highest executive power, and that is how the HVO was formed at the municipality level. This occurred on the 10th of July already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the first president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: So the official authorities were renamed to become the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When these municipal governments were formed at the HVO level, how did the Muslims behave? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of July in '92, in Vitez, the Croatian Defence Council was formed as a civil authority in order to carry out preparations in the best possible way for defence from aggression and preparations for the winter in that sense, and this was, in fact, an executive authority. The Muslims were offered the option to join the authority in accordance with the proportional votes from the elections, and these negotiations lasted about a month, even longer than that, but they refused to join this government and they formed a parallel government. These governments were operating in the same building for about a month, and then after that they withdrew and separated and went to a different location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Mahala you want to say?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the government separated did the police separate as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: You asked me before that who the President was of the Croatian Defence Council. The first president was the same president, former president of the municipality, Mr. Ivan Santic. And his deputy, as far as the organisation went, was Mr. Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us -- answer what I asked you about the police? Was there a division among the police as well between the two sides?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no division right away but after a certain time, yes, the police divided too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many kinds of police were there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: At that time already there were four kinds of police, military police within the HVO, civil police within HVO, and then military police within the BH army, the Muslim side, and the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So two civilian police forces and two military police forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we are talking about this, could we talk about the health centre? Was there a health centre in -- health clinic in Vitez, and was this an institution for both Muslims and for Croats or was there a separation there as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: There was a health clinic in Vitez. It was of quite a considerable size. It was an institution that was a joint institution for both Croats and Muslims until serious conflicts started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the economy like at that time after the authorities were formed? What was the financial make-up?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council, when it was formed, the situation within the economic sector was serious already, and in that sense the government of the Croatian Defence Council determined priorities at that time, as a priority how to resolve and stabilise the situation in the economy. First of all, given the political and military circumstances, how to resolve the key problems such as the problem of provision for the supplies for the population. And in order to resolve this problem of supplying the citizens, which was a very important problem, it was essential to resolve on a priority basis the completion of certain communications through which the required quantities of food and other necessities could be delivered. So we were working on this link, this communication. We invested a lot of funds and efforts in that, and we called it the 'Saviour's Path.' So the construction of the path of salvation was begun in order to provide enough food and other essential things that were, first of all, primarily required for defence from aggression. This -- it was reported by the media that the Serb forces were seriously thinking about joining their forces from Vlasic, through the Lasva Valley, with the forces which were already in Kobiljaca in front of Sarajevo. So in such circumstances, the situation, the spirit among the people, the mood among the people was exceptionally bad. Panic was among the people. The situation on the market was already such that it looked like anything but like a normal situation. The Croatia Defence Council, through its supply unit, was thinking about ways to resolve this problem, including, of course, engaging other departments, such as the Department of the Economy, and others to resolve some problems within their jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we discuss the make-up of the HVO government for the Court to have a better view, what were the duties -- what were your duties at the time in the HVO government?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I was a representative from the -- I was head of the supply division in the HVO government, and it was logical for this department to be within the economical department, but HVO government felt that the supply problem deserved serious thought and that it should be formed as a special separate department. So I was in charge of this supply department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perform any other duties except for the ones related to supply? Can you tell us anything about humanitarian aid and what were your duties regarding that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Within the HVO government there was a department for refugees and displaced persons, and we accepted and distributed humanitarian aid in our department. So it was my job to try to resolve the problem of supply. As far as humanitarian aid is concerned, at that time I did not have complete data, but I know that very little aid actually arrived in order to meet the needs of the population and the growing number of refugees at that time. For that reason I would like to go back again to the duties -- to my duties. The HVO government entrusted me with finding ways of how to resolve the problem of the growing requirements for supply. In view of the overall military and political situation was the way I mentioned before, and the fact that the HVO government did not have a lot of funds at its disposal, together with the chief of the economics department, I proposed ways on -- to resolve the problem of supply. We decided to offer a sort of winter package of the most necessary winter goods in order to bridge this period until springtime, and in order to bridge the longest possible period. So the HVO government offered a package of the most important provisions and was looking for the most favourable offers, and announced to the public that it would guarantee the delivery of these provisions and that the citizens would need to pay in advance for this. This was the only realistic option to ensure the greatest amounts of provisions in the shortest possible time to satisfy the needs of the citizens and to resolve the problems that I discussed. So in a very brief time, thanks to the fact that there were a lot of private businessmen in Vitez who were successful traders, we asked for bids for these goods. And when I talk about strategic goods I mean flour, oil, salt, potatoes. So in a month we managed to receive enough bids so that we could offer the citizens these goods with the guarantee of the HVO that the provisions would be delivered before the onset of winter. So we had to work very quickly, because it is well-known that the communications already in October and November could become impassable. So based on some 7.700 households in Vitez, we estimated that we needed to ensure 1.5 million kilogrammes of goods for winter provisions. Before that, the economics department recommended that maximum number quantities of these goods should be ensured for their workers, for their employees, so that in September the situation was much different regarding the provision of citizens. The winter provision was carried out quite successfully, so that the majority of citizens in Vitez had sufficient quantities of goods and could safely await the winter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, when you talk about provisions, were Muslims and Croats equally supplied with these goods?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. The policy of the HVO government was to supply all the citizens of Vitez, because only in that way could it be counted on good interethnic relations that peace could be preserved, and in that sense the President of the HVO government, Mr. Santic, and myself had the need and the task to carry out this work to mutual satisfaction. And this job was carried out for all the citizens of Vitez, and I think that the participation in this winter provision -- there was a little less supply that went to the Muslims than it did to the Croats, because the number of Muslims who had applied was less than the number of Croats, but they did accept this with a certain amount of doubt, but it started off successfully and this number grew so there was -- there was no problem on that side to accept these supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have already mentioned the question of humanitarian aid. As far as you know, did humanitarian organisations such as Caritas and Merhamet, were they active in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course they operated. The first humanitarian organisation that was active in Vitez was the municipal, the county Caritas organisation, and it started its activities very early. It was the only organisation to be active in Vitez right until '92. Then in '92 Merhamet was formed, at the time when a lot of expelled Muslims arrived in Vitez. So Merhamet was formed as an organisation. There was a need for them to have their own humanitarian organisation which would meet the growing needs of the expelled persons, whose number was growing daily. In the beginning, I know that Caritas also provided for both the needs of the Muslims and the Croats as much as it was possible. In '92, in the second half of '92, other humanitarian organisations appeared, such as the High Commissioner and the Red Cross, and they were active in that region, but this was, as I said, insufficient in order to provide for the needs of the citizens and to reduce tensions and the fears about approaching winter and how to live through the period of winter in view of the fact that the overall military and political situation was very serious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We spoke here about the relations between Muslims and Croats and aid. Did you know that after the formation of the HVO authorities there was a coordinating committee for the protection of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know about that. It was formed maybe about a month after the formation of the HVO, this body, the coordinating committee for the protection of the interests of Muslims was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the objective of that committee? What does it mean, the protection of Muslims? What's the intention?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I think this was a way to achieve or implement parallel power, at least that's how I understood it, because it did happen that parallel authorities were being formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were a lot of refugees in Vitez and this humanitarian organisation Merhamet was formed. Were there more refugees in Vitez? Were there more Muslim or Croat refugees in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as refugees are concerned in Vitez, this can be viewed or should be viewed according to the different periods. At the beginning of '92, after the fall of Kupres and other parts of Bosnia such as Kotor Varos, the number of refugees was more or less the same, but as time went on, as we went on later into '92 in Vitez and particularly after the fall of Jajce, the opposite situation occurred in Vitez, there was a much greater number of Muslim refugees in Vitez, and this can also apply to the whole of Central Bosnia. Already by November, after the fall of Jajce, the situation was obvious, that a large number of Bosnia and Herzegovina was occupied, the greatest part was practically cleansed of Croats and Serbs, and then in this period, from the second half of '92 until the end of '92, the greatest number of refugees of Muslim nationality came to Central Bosnia and then, in large numbers, they also came to Vitez. It was estimated at that time that there were about 4.500 to 5.000 refugees of Muslim nationality and about 1.000 to 1.500 Croatian refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, among the refugees who came to Central Bosnia, especially to Vitez, were there any able-bodied men, especially among the Muslim refugees, men fit for military duty?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, there were able-bodied men fit for military duty. It's estimated that only in Central Bosnia there were about 80.000 Muslims from -- were estimated to have arrived in Central Bosnia, about 80.000 Muslims, and this was a greater number than the total number of Croats in Central Bosnia. So it is certain that amongst such a large number of refugees, there were a lot of able-bodied men and also a large number of armed persons. Looking at it from a broader aspect, the largest number of Muslim refugees were in Central Bosnia. There was a smaller number of Croats. I know that in Jajce, all the Croats had left and all the Muslims had stayed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all the Croats had left and all the Muslims had stayed in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the situation for Zenica, Busovaca, Travnik, but also for Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we will go back to the composition of the government. So if you could please tell us about the composition of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The government was organised, as I mentioned in the beginning, it was organised in departments. There were several departments, and the key departments at that time were the department for economy, department for supply, as I said, then department for national defence, civil police affairs, department for the land books, legal questions, social affairs, and also the general administration department. So there were about nine or ten departments. There was a department for displaced persons, for refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where that government was based?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The seat of the government was in the municipal building where the government was organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where the government was permanently?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the government was there until the outbreak of hostilities, and then it was transferred to a different location because the building was shelled and there were no conditions there for normal operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the president of the government then and -- you already mentioned Ivan Santic and Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the government permanently in session? Were all the members of the government present at their meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The government had meetings or was in session frequently in view of the fact that there were a lot of problems. I most frequently attended these government meetings, but it happened sometimes that because of my other duties, I would miss meetings. So it was in session. They passed around information about the current problems, the ways to resolve them, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the government make decisions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they made decisions at the level of the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what other levels were decisions made?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The decisions were made, decisions, conclusions, recommendations were made at the government level, but most often recommendations were made at the level of the department because the departments were quite independent in carrying out their duties, and there was a need occasionally to exchange information and to provide information to the government about what has been carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the president was Ivan Santic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ivan Santic was president of the HVO government all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he president of the crisis committee as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Santic, according to his post, was also president of the crisis committee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever make decisions on his own without the government?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did have that option, and he probably did make the decisions alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We mentioned here the department for defence. What was the task, the duty, what were the duties of the Vitez defence department?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The duties of the Vitez defence department were to organise all the documentation pertaining to military conscripts, also according to need to carry out mobilisation. I think that it also contacted the village guards initially and then later to organise the military conscripts, maintain lists of military conscripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the role of the department was mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was its role.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the mobilisation was carried out by filling in the ranks?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the job is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing as a member of the government regarding mobilisation? What was your task? In the government, you said you did not deal with the military questions but your duties had to do with the supply.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my duties throughout that period were regarding the problems of supplies. I did not have anything to do with military questions except sometimes I had the opportunity to hear some information about the situation in the other departments. So my tasks from the very beginning, right until the cease-fire with the Muslims, was always the same, all the way until the Dayton accords, and if I may add, at the beginning of the war, besides supplies, my duties also included the coordination of humanitarian aid at the beginning of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we will go back. Do you remember the first conflict on the 20th of October in '92?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I had the opportunity to receive information at an HVO government meeting that at a road between Vitez and Busovaca, barricades were put up by certain armed groups of Muslims. An attempt was made to have the roadblock removed by peaceful means, but these talks were not successful and the roadblock was removed by force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any houses destroyed and was anyone killed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: A serious resistance was put up. There was an exchange of fire and, as a result, several houses were damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was an agreement on reconciliation reached and an agreement to repair the houses?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the barricade was removed, I think that during the working hours of that same day, a truce was agreed on, and the proposal was made or, rather, an agreement was reached that every effort be made to repair the damaged houses as soon as possible so that they can be used again, and I think that this was successfully resolved a few days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will proceed now immediately to the conflict of the 16th of April, '93, but before then, could you list the incidents that occurred in the meantime, if you could, the incidents between the Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Before the roadblock, I know that, on the 17th or the 18th, a roadblock was put up on the road between Travnik and Novi Travnik and that this roadblock was put there by the Muslims, and during attempts to have it removed, again there was fire exchanged, and I think that an assistant commander of the HVO in Travnik was killed and another person who was there during attempts to agree to appease the situation and remove the barricade. I also know that there were a number of incidents in Novi Travnik or, rather, that -- but these were successfully overcome, and also I think it was on the 19th or maybe the 18th, a conflict of broader proportions occurred in Novi Travnik. Actually, a shelling occurred and exchange of heavy gunfire, and this went on for some time, even after the roadblock was removed between Vitez and Busovaca. I also know that the military police in Travnik was attacked, it was housed in the music school, and before that, maybe -- some time before that, there was an incident in Kiseljak and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that brings us to the 16th of April, 1993. Where were you on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, I was at work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the 16th of April, '93? How did you learn that a conflict had occurred?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I learnt about it because I was awakened by the sound of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was this?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: This was about 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a member of the HVO government, what was your duty after that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the day, I was called in by the president of the HVO, Mr. Santic, to try to come to work so that we could discuss the question of organisation of supply, but I answered that I would not be able to come unless there was a lull in the fighting, and, in fact, I managed to get there on the 17th, and I was given my regular assignment there to organise the supply of both citizens and the soldiers, if the conflict should continue. Therefore, I couldn't go immediately when I was called in, but I did manage to get there the next day and to meet with Mr. Santic who gave me this assignment to try and organise supply in spite of the circumstances and to try and organise the collection of potatoes that had arrived for planting, and we discussed all these matters very briefly. He simply gave me the task to try and organise all questions related to supply despite the circumstances and, if the conflict should continue, to find a way to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were unable to get there, how did you communicate with him?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I communicated by telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Ivan Santic spoke to other employees and did he give them other assignments on that day?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The telephone lines were functioning. He informed me that it was nothing abnormal, that I had to try and continue doing my work because each of the members of the government had their responsibilities to perform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Ivica Santic inform you whether he had informed other members of the government of their assignments?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I was afraid then, but he said, "Don't be afraid. The situation is such as it is, and all the heads of departments are duty-bound to organise the activities within their department," and that meant myself as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that a conflict would occur on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You just said that you were awakened by the sound of shooting. We have a few more questions relating to the 16th of April. Do you know the casualty figure for Ahmici? Were you informed about it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me assist you. There's a list of the dead, but you said that this was not in your domain. But let me ask you something else: Do you know how Civil Defence functioned before the 16th of April and after the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as Civil Defence is concerned, it was frequently a topic of discussion at meetings of the HVO, and I know that, even at the end of '91 and '92, it was relatively well-organised so that there were Civil Defence representatives in each village, and, if necessary, in fact, there were several representatives in the same village, depending on the size of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether men were recruited to the Civil Defence and what exactly they did on the 16th of April, 1993? Did anyone inform you as a member of the government?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I was informed that the Civil Defence had been given its own assignments, just like any other department, and its assignment was certainly to organise itself. How it did so, I really couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the task of the Civil Defence on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the normal task of Civil Defence was to take care of civilians, women, children, and to do rehabilitation and rebuilding if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the HVO government was the decision-maker. Did any one of the accused participate in that decision-making process?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The accused here present. Did any one of them participate in the decision-making of the HVO government?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course not. Not any one of the accused could have, nor did they participate in the decision-making at the level of the HVO government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they participate in the negotiations between the Croats and Muslims on important issues such as exchange of prisoners, removal of barricades and the like?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Personally, I think that they did not, because simply they didn't hold any such positions. As for their participation in the work of the HVO government or any influence on the government, I really don't know, or, rather, I don't think they could have had any influence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did make those decision?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: What decisions are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the level of the HVO government, and who among the Croats took part in the negotiations on the major issues with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever important issues were discussed, the President of the Crisis Staff would participate, that is Mr. Santic, frequently the Deputy President Mr. Skopljak. Depending on the nature of the question discussed. If we were working on a relaxation of tensions, then some representative of the military would take part as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the Muslims and Croats would reach an agreement, would the Croats observe those decisions? I'm thinking of the decisions signed by HVO representatives.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, most frequently they would observe those decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: There were cases when agreements were not carried through. Even after the 20th of October, for instance, in spite of the fact that the situation was successfully overcome, there were a number of incidents, but on both sides attempts were made to calm the situation down, and in most cases successfully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Croats were also among the casualties of the war. Could you tell us where the Croats were victims, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and in the surroundings, and perhaps in the direction of Busovaca. Do you know where Buhine Kuce is?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The second most serious incident was the killing, with a shell, of six or seven children. In fact, two were wounded and, in fact, they died. So the total number of victims was eight children. Then there was the casualty figure in Buhine Kuce or Krizancevo Selo, where a total of 66 people were affected, out of which 34 were captured, but they were also exchanged, some of them were killed. Then in Buhine Kuce again there were five or six casualties again, some of them killed. The first incident involving casualties in Central Bosnia occurred in the municipality of Dusina in Busovaca when the Muslim forces attacked Busovaca. I think some 15 or 16 civilians were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Muslims and Croats were exchanged between Zenica and Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I know that there were attempts to carry out exchanges at the beginning of the war -- or, rather the conflict. At least that was the information I received at one of the government meetings, that this attempt ended in such a way that all the Muslims who in the initial stages of the conflict were released home and were given the freedom to go where they wanted, whereas the agreement reached at the UNPROFOR base in Stari Bila, no Muslims came from Zenica as a result of that agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who participated in those talks on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: In the first round the talks, as far as I know it was Mr. Skopljak and the commander of the Vitez Brigade, Mr. Mario Cerkez. That was in the UNPROFOR base, the first round of talks. Mr. Skopljak, several days after the conflict, was dealing with the questions of exchange not only at the level of Vitez, but at the level of the whole of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic (sic), you were a member of the government. Perhaps you could tell us why the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats actually occurred, and could you please give us the causes of that conflict?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, the war -- or, rather, the conflict occurred for a number of reasons. I have mentioned some of them, and let me repeat it. First of all, the inertia on behalf of the Muslims, and the official policy in relation to the aggression against Croatia. President Izetbegovic, at the time, said that it wasn't our war, that it was a war between the Serbs and the Croats. Then there was the decision taken by the official authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina on their neutrality regarding the aggression. Then the military/political developments in'92, and the actual aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the influx of a large number of displaced persons to Central Bosnia, including Vitez. The presence of two armies, one might call them, relatively well armed on a relatively small space. The balance between the Muslims and the Croats in the total population was roughly seven to one. It is estimated that in the period from the beginning of 1993, there was a large influx of Muslim displaced persons, among whom many came relatively well armed. So that the ratio, the population ratio, certainly affected and contributed to the conflict. In my personal view, the position of the top level military leadership was that the Croats could very simply be subdued, because judging by many incidents that occurred in Vitez or within the Lasva River Valley as a whole, it was visible that activities were being coordinated from the highest level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you said that the Croats could be easily subdued? Are you referring to the large number of well-armed displaced persons and able-bodied Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I already said that the ratio was roughly seven to one in favour of the Muslims, and this in itself was an important factor, in my personal opinion. So in the broader region of Central Bosnia, they were quite well organised and quite well armed, and that this option was a viable one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have seen that the BH army did not capture Vitez, but it did capture Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf and Fojnica. Could you tell us why that was so, bearing in mind that Bugojno is linked to Kupres, which is of major military significance for this area?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not capture Vitez, as you said, but it did capture most of Vitez. But the HVO, after the truce was agreed with the Muslims, controlled about 35 per cent only, and this could roughly be said for other municipalities like Novi Travnik, where they held about 40 per cent, as far as I know. Also in Busovaca. But only 15 per cent of Travnik remained under HVO control. Therefore, the BH army did control most of Central Bosnia, pushing the Croats into small limited areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention Kiseljak, which is also populated mostly by Croats.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the situation in Kiseljak was more or less the same, but at the beginning the conflict in Busovaca, sometime in January, I know that Busovaca was virtually divided into two parts, the dividing line going through Kacuni. That is how the forces were divided too, along a length of some 10 to 12 kilometres, maybe 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you to explain how it was that Vitez found itself surrounded, and what did the Muslims intend to do with Vitez in view of the fact that Bugojno had fell and that it had been captured by the Muslims? What was their intention? Because we know how Bugojno fell, Gornji Vakuf and Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Since I said that the highest military leadership felt that this would be relatively easy prey and they tried to capture it, and they were more or less successful, not only in Vitez, the Lasva Valley, but throughout Central Bosnia. My personal view is that an area of several -- if there had been a passage of a few kilometres through which people could have left, then they would have achieved their goal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us what their intention was. In other words, to achieve the same as they did in Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf and Fojnica. Could you tell us whether the Croats were chased out of these three towns?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Croats from Bugojno -- you asked me, "How did you explain" -- "How would you explain that Bugojno fell?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, because it is linked to Kupres and it has a better position than Vitez.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: It is rather difficult to explain, but clearly Bugojno, at least as far as I know, judging from meetings of the HVO, Bugojno was relatively well armed, but it was defeated by the BH army even though it has Croatian enclaves behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were saying that you were surrounded and you had no other choice but to fight until the end?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Already in May, as far as I can remember, we were totally surrounded and there was absolutely no way out of Vitez. The only solution was to defend ourselves and fight for survival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us whether the Muslims wanted to put you under even greater strain by cutting off the main road?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so. This was a very narrow area, and the strategy was to try and separate the forces between Busovaca and Vitez, and that was the gist of the strategy applied. I believe that if they had succeeded in cutting off Busovaca and Vitez, or dividing Vitez into two, there would have -- probably the forces would have had to surrender. However, thanks to the factory that we had and the amount of ammunition available to us that we could use for defence, as far as I have been informed, we managed successfully to resist attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago the 16th of April. Do you know whether any Croats were killed in Ahmici, or did you know any of the dead?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know that on the first day -- actually, I learned several days after the conflict that five people were killed, and I know one of the men killed, Mirjan Santic, and I know a very young man who was killed from Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the young man from Rijeka, but I know that Mirjan Santic was in the military police. I don't know the names of the others who were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were listing the reasons of the war, you referred to a statement made by Alija Izetbegovic and the others. Were there any arrests of Croats in the period preceding the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did manage that some incidents occurred. There was tension. A group was intercepted in Kruscica, and they were taken into custody and beaten up, but nevertheless these difficulties were overcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're referring to the period prior to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, prior to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of the case of Zivko Totic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that Mr. Zivko Totic, on the 15th -- or, rather, that he was a HVO commander in Zenica, and on the 15th he was intercepted by Muslim forces, and that all the members of his escort were killed and he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there negotiations for him to be released?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These were conducted by Mr. Pero Skopljak, and I know there was an exchange but I couldn't tell you when nor whom he was exchanged for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, as it is time for the break, with your permission I would suggest we take a break now because I will have another ten minutes of questioning, or shall I continue with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, no. Let's take a break, a 30-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, we left off at Zivko Totic before the break, so could you please tell us whether he was released and returned to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know that after the initial stage of the conflict, this was done. I don't know exactly when, maybe 15 or 20 days, maybe longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before, when you were responding to my questions, and since you were the head of the supply department, perhaps it would be a good thing if you explained to us the taxation system while you were a member of the government.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Since, in the period when the HVO government was formed, the financial organisation that was in force then completely fell apart, and other organisations also fell apart, the economy and everything else, the municipality was practically in the situation of trying to resolve the taxation system on its own in order to get some funds. So the Croatian Defence Council, the finance department in fact, issued recommendations on the way to resolve this issue, meaning how to tax products. I remember that these taxes were much lower than in normal circumstances in view of the fact that the social situation of the population and all the other conditions were very serious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your work had to do with trade as a profession, and then you were in the supply department.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. For a while, I worked in the commerce department, for three years, and then from 1979 until the end of the elections, I worked in my company, which was actually dealing with the supply of the citizens of Vitez, which it did before the war as well. In a municipality the size of Vitez, this would be one company whose job would be to supply the citizens in wholesale and retail. So in this sense, I worked in the retail department and then I worked in the wholesale department in the basic organisation of associated labour whose job it was to deal with wholesale. I worked in a company which was based in Zenica, but the unit of that company was in Vitez. So I worked in this job before I took on the other duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were a member of the HVO, you said that the government had frequent sessions. Did you always attend these important meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not attend the meetings always. It depends on which period we are talking about. When I was dealing with the problem of supply that I discussed earlier, and this would be the period of August, September, and October, and when I was busy with that, I did not always attend the meetings because I had a lot to do trying to fulfil the obligations that I had, and I tried to do that in the way that I thought best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you submit reports to the government on this issue, on supplying of the population in this region?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The frequent topic of discussion was the problem of supply that I talked about, so I did submit reports on a number of occasions, particularly in the period that we were actively dealing with the problem of supplying the population in order to go through the winter of '92-'93 as best as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were head of the supply department, did you coordinate, did you provide logistics to the HVO or the Vitez Brigade? Was that one of your duties, you know, when mobilisation is going on, and then did you have anything to do regarding the logistics?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the government had that task, to assure certain supplies for the military units. At the start of the conflict, as I said before, since the conflict did not stop, I was entrusted with the job of providing certain quantities of food for the needs of logistics besides supplying the population, so it was my job to obtain certain quantities and deliver them to the units or to the brigade, and that's where my duties ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you did not attend all the meetings. Did you work out on the ground, and what were your duties if you were out on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I was out on the ground a lot, and when we were actively dealing with the problem to provide winter supplies, I did tour a number of villages, explaining what was being offered in the package, what strategic goods were being offered to the citizens, the terms; and on several occasions, I also visited Muslim villages, explaining in the same way the offer, so that we would gain the trust and the confidence, and we got that pretty quickly because the first delivery was successfully carried out. So I did go out on the ground to make the offer and also when distribution was being carried out, and then during the war, I went out on the ground to organise the sowing, and also I bought certain agricultural products and cattle, and I would deliver that to the logistics unit for the needs of the military units. Of course, I did not do this myself. My department had a number of employees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you obtained these goods. Could you please tell us where you obtained the goods from, from which regions? Did you obtain the goods from outside of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You could only get the goods, at the stage that I was talking about, exclusively from outside of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because at that stage, in May, June, July and the months after that, Bosnia and Herzegovina was very badly supplied on the whole, and except in parts of Herzegovina, you could not obtain goods, so the goods were mainly obtained from Croatia, sometimes imported but mostly from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you obtained the goods from Croatia, how did you ensure safe passage of those goods?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Already at that time, in October and November, regarding the security situation, it wasn't very safe, but this was nevertheless being organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how this was organised?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Goods were obtained -- as I said, in Vitez, we had a number of companies who were able to obtain the required quantities pretty efficiently. This is confirmed by the fact that in the period from March to October '92, a period when we were efficiently and actively organising the supply of winter goods through the companies, and we managed to cut in half the prices of strategic goods on the market. So that the price of flour, for example, in March or April, was 1.20 German marks, but in our package, it was offered at 55 pfennigs, and we did ensure the required quantities, stabilised the market, and ensured sufficient quantities so that they could be bought in retail at a price of 60 pfennig. To my surprise, when I look at that from today's point of view, prices are now higher than they were in September-October '92. Of course, during the conflict itself, as it went on, there were shortages of goods; then the situation was worse than it was in '92, at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Muslims and Croats able to buy these goods in the same way, meaning at the same prices?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that we made the offer for all citizens of Vitez, including, of course, all nationalities, and Muslims among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to say something else?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: So this was something that was done for all the citizens of Vitez, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I would like the usher -- we are going to move to another question now, so I would like to ask the usher to show you document D32/2. I would like the usher to give the witness the translation of the document. The witness doesn't speak English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: He has the B/C/S version in front of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, this is a report, an announcement, as you can see. Have you seen this announcement before?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, some of this I am familiar with. I see here the representatives of the UNHCR, UNPROFOR, representatives of the religious communities, commanders of the armed forces of the B and H army, representatives of the HVO, Ivo Santic and Mr. Pero Skopljak and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pero Skopljak and Ivan Santic, who were they representing?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Pero Skopljak and Ivan Santic were representing the Croatian Defence Council, and most frequently they took part in the meetings of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides them, who else participated on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Most often a representative of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I see here, Mario Cerkez in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Ivan Santic and Pero Skopljak always take part in the negotiations with the Muslim side in such situations and similar situations?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mostly it was Mr. Santic, frequently Mr. Skopljak, these people that we see on this document now, in announcements about agreements to calm the situation regarding the barricades on the road between Vitez and Busovaca and regarding the overall situation at that time between the two sides. In this case, I see Friar Anto Tomas here, I don't know him that much, and Mr. Omer Efendija Mestrovac, representative of the Muslim community of the Islamic community. I don't know that they participated in meetings often, but on this occasion, I see that they did, because this was probably a more serious situation and an attempt to engage representatives of all the important sides, including representatives of the religious communities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these talks and agreements happen often?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thinking from the 16th of October, '92, to April 16th, '93.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these contacts were frequent, after any kind of incident occurred, and this is also confirmed by the fact that relatively tolerable relations were maintained up until the 16th of April in '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the announcements and the meetings and the negotiations, do you understand this, that from the conflict in Busovaca, all the way until the 16th of April, '93, there were no serious clashes?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This attests to the fact that there were people in Vitez from both sides who managed to maintain relatively tolerable relations, even after the conflict in Busovaca in January, even though it went on for two or three months, thanks to the correct approach, the attitude of both sides, which managed to maintain such relations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Pero Skopljak frequently took part in the talks and negotiations. What were his duties in the government?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: He was the vice-president of the Croatian Defence Council and he maintained contacts in situations when this was not required, besides Mr. Santic, who was mostly present at all negotiations when this was called for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides Ivan Santic and Pero Skopljak, in talks while reaching -- did other people who were not members of the government, with the exception of members of the religious community or the military community, did these persons also participate in the decision-making process?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody took a part in the decision-making process other than representatives of the HVO government, especially not representatives of the religious community. When we're talking about decisions of any kind, they were made within the HVO government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These decisions made by the HVO government, were they observed? Were they observed and were they observed -- these decisions, were they observed also by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: The majority of the decisions by the HVO government, particularly in the period since it was formed and on, were mostly observed. They were frequently observed with a certain degree of respect by the Muslims. But when we talked about the tolerable relations which we maintained until April 16th, this was done thanks to the president of the HVO government as well as other members, depending on the area that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the HVO government made decisions and reached agreements with the Muslim side and say there was a problem in one of the villages of the Vitez municipality, were these decisions binding on all sides, the village and in the town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, decisions by the HVO government were binding on all the citizens of Vitez, including all the regions of Vitez, so in this sense, including the villages and the hamlets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the decisions of the HVO government were observed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the usher give the witness document 339, D339?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, do you mean D39/2?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I think it's marked D339. I may have written it down, but it could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It's a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I think it's P. I apologise, Your Honour. Yes, it's P339.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see, Mr. Alilovic, what is this about?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, who signed this joint statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: This joint statement was signed by Mr. Santic on behalf of Croatian community. This was a joint statement by representatives of the Croats and Muslims in the municipality of Vitez. At that time Mr. Muhamed Mujezinovic, before the conflict as far as I know, was, on the Muslims' side, one of the persons in the government body. In any case this was a statement that I had the opportunity to hear either on the radio or see on the local television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mujezinovic by profession?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Mujezinovic was a doctor, and I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about him, about his activities at that time and his authority within the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to say first that we went to elementary school together, that we studied in Sarajevo at the same time, and Mr. Mujezinovic, I don't know exactly what year, but after completing his studies he didn't immediately start working in Vitez. He came to Vitez, and as a doctor, a general practitioner, he worked there first. Then in occupational medicine he was working in a factory for industrial explosives, and he was known all over the community. He had the authority and enjoyed a good reputation among the Muslim people at the stage when this was called for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to item 5 of the joint statement, where reference is made to the civilian bodies of government at the highest level, which are required immediately to establish an ongoing political dialogue until the establishment of peace and the establishment of authority in the provinces and in the municipalities. Was that a suggestion or was it a recommendation? How would you describe it? Was it an order, because the term "It is requested," is used? How was this decision implemented?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I personally think that this was a recommendation expressing the wish to make another attempt, and I think that the wish was sincere on the part of both to try to halt the hostilities through the mediation of the civilian and military authorities so that the conflict would not continue, because both of these people must have been fully aware of the consequences. Therefore, I think that they were prompted by the sincere wish to try and do everything possible to end the hostilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic (sic), under item 5, will you tell us in what capacity did Ivan Santic sign this statement, because no title is given here?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: He signed it as a representative -- as the president of the Crisis Staff and the president of the HVO. As for Muhamed, as the representative of the wartime government of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, let me ask you: When this joint statement was drafted, did Ivan Santic ask for permission from the HVO government to sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. As I said, I heard the statement read out on our local television. As far as I can recall, both of them spoke on television, and this programme could be seen by most of the citizens of both Croat and Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivan Santic, as the president of the municipality and the head of the Crisis Staff, did he have any authority, without the support of the government, to pass important decisions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. He had the authority, and, in fact, I think he did take decisions that I am not aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were similar decisions made by his deputy, Mr. Pero Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He too had certain competencies in that respect to make decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what area?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Primarily in the area of exchange. He acted independently at the time. At least as far as I know, he was the person in charge of exchanges, not only for the municipality of Vitez but for the whole area of Central Bosnia, and he was authorised to negotiate independently and also to take decisions independently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he take such decisions on his own when exchanges were carried out, exchanges of civilians, and even exchanges of the dead, because we know that there were, unfortunately, even exchanges of bodies. Was he independent in making decisions in both these areas?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, he would consult with the president, but in the final stage and in the course of the negotiations he would decide on his own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About exchanges?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher to show the witness document P335, please? Mr. Santic --

utterances.speaker: VLADO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Alilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
